subject: Post-call recap — Aurelia on-prem constraints, handoff and next actions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Isaac Turner <isaac.turner@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-07T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — Aurelia on-prem constraints, handoff and next actions

Isaac / Aurelia team,

Thanks again for the call today — helpful to understand the constraints up front. Key points I captured:

- Target deployment model: fully air-gapped on-prem appliance in Aurelia's primary research datacenter (no egress to public internet).
- Data residency: all model artifacts and inference telemetry must remain on-site; no telemetry forwarding to Redwood-hosted control plane unless explicitly approved.
- KMS: prefer customer-managed HSM for keys on-prem; if unavailable, we discussed an offline-encrypted key import flow.
- Upgrades: must support offline upgrade media (signed artifacts), and upgrade windows are limited to UTC 02:00–06:00 local time with a 2-hour blackout for critical experiments.
- Hardware constraints: single 42U rack footprint, up to 4x GPUs (NVIDIA A100 40GB preferred), limited external I/O (no vendor remote console unless via jump-host).

Requested next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll send an initial on-prem requirements doc and a trimmed network diagram for your infra team to validate (attached).
2) Marissa / Jonas — can you produce a first-pass offline upgrade runbook (MOP) and a short canary plan we can share with Aurelia?
3) Isaac — please confirm whether Aurelia will provide an on-site HSM or want us to include a signed-import path. Also confirm the blackout window timezone (your local ops team mentioned Pacific?).

Attachments: redwood-onprem-reqs-v1.pdf (summary of constraints and minimal HW list), network-diagram-aurelia.png (sketch from today).

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up with your infra team next week if that helps.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

---
Attachment stubs: redwood-onprem-reqs-v1.pdf (PDF, 6 pages) ; network-diagram-aurelia.png (PNG, 1 image)
From: Isaac Turner <isaac.turner@aureliatx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurelia Tech Ops <infra@aureliatx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-08T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Aurelia on-prem constraints, handoff and next actions

Ben — thanks for the summary and for the attachments. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed: Pacific local time for the blackout window (UTC-7 during DST). The lab schedule means the 02:00–06:00 window may need to be narrowed to 02:00–04:00 for the first phase.
- HSM: We do have an on-site HSM cluster but the team prefers no remote key import. If Redwood needs keys pre-loaded, we can do it via signed USB media during install. Is there an accepted format for the signed artifact?
- Firmware signing: Our security team requires that all upgrade images be signed by an issuer we trust (we can provide a root CA). Can you confirm Redwood’s signing practice and whether you can produce artifacts signed with a customer-provided CA?
- Hardware: we are evaluating 3x A100 40GB (space/Cooling constraints) rather than 4x. Is that supported for the initial PoC throughput target (10 qps @ 512 tokens)?

Also — please include a brief checklist we can give our facilities team for rack power/cooling and a list of installed OS-level packages required for the appliance.

Appreciate it,
Isaac Turner
Director, Infrastructure — Aurelia Therapeutics
isaac.turner@aureliatx.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-08T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Internal — Aurelia next actions (MOP + canary plan)

Marissa / Jonas — following up to assign tasks from the Aurelia call and Isaac’s clarifications. Summary and suggested owners: 

- Offline upgrade/process (MOP): Marissa — draft a 1–2 page MOP that covers: signed artifact verification, USB/media import steps, rollback, pre-upgrade checks (DB snapshots, model artifact backups), and post-upgrade verification. Target: first draft by 2028-06-10 EOD.
- Canary plan + sizing guidance: Jonas — produce a short canary run (3-step plan: smoke test, controlled traffic ramp, SLA check) that validates 3x A100 40GB meets their 10 qps @ 512 tokens target. Include expected latency and cost delta vs. 4x config. Target: 2028-06-11 COB.
- Facilities checklist: I’ll adapt our standard rack checklist into a 1-page handout for Aurelia facilities (power per PDU, breaker requirements, RU reservations, recommended intake airflow).

Blockers/questions: please confirm whether our signed-image format is acceptable to them (Isaac asked about CA-signed artifacts). I’ll also ask Product about signing flow if you need a quick primer.

Thanks — let’s sync for 20 mins tomorrow if either of you needs alignment.

Ben
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Isaac Turner <isaac.turner@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Aurelia Tech Ops <infra@aureliatx.com>
Date: 2028-06-09T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Aurelia on-prem constraints, handoff and next actions

Isaac — quick update and answers to your questions: 

1) Upgrade signing and CA: Redwood can produce artifacts signed with a customer-provided root CA. We’ll need the root certificate and an agreed subject to embed in the signature during PoC. I’ll open a PKI ticket and include the exact format we support (PKCS7 detached + SHA256).

2) Hardware sizing: 3x A100 40GB is supported for the PoC target you gave (10 qps @ 512 tokens). Jonas will provide an expected latency envelope and where we would recommend adding a 4th GPU for headroom.

3) Offline key import: we support a signed key import path via encrypted USB media; our MOP will document the verification steps and checksums.

4) Facilities checklist: attached is a one-page rack & power checklist adapted for Aurelia (power draw, single-LAN jump-host requirement, and recommended RU).

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa will share MOP draft by 2028-06-10.
- Jonas will share canary sizing + expected latency report by 2028-06-11.
- Proposed follow-up call with your infra team: 2028-06-14 09:00–09:30 PT — does that work?

If that timing doesn’t work, suggest two alternatives and we’ll accommodate.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to an on-site scoping PoC.

Best,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
